pr.title: For async closures, cap closure kind, get rid of `by_mut_body`
pr.description:
Right now we have three `AsyncFn*` traits, and three corresponding futures that are returned by the `call_*` functions for them. This is fine, but it is a bit excessive, since the future returned by `AsyncFn` and `AsyncFnMut` are identical. Really, the only distinction we need to make with these bodies is "by ref" and "by move".

This PR removes `AsyncFn::CallFuture` and renames `AsyncFnMut::CallMutFuture` to `AsyncFnMut::CallRefFuture`. This simplifies MIR building for async closures, since we don't need to build an extra "by mut" body, but just a "by move" body which is materially different.

We need to do a bit of delicate handling of the ClosureKind for async closures, since we need to "cap" it to `AsyncFnMut` in some cases when we only care about what body we're looking for.

This also fixes a bug where `<{async closure} as Fn>::call` was returning a body that takes the async-closure receiver *by move*.

This also helps align the `AsyncFn` traits to the `LendingFn` traits' eventual designs.

analysis.summary: Historical PR 05116c5c..+f1fef64e..+541858ed fixes async-closure MIR/ABI handling while also removing a redundant coroutine body. Before the change, async closures tracked three `AsyncFn*` futures and generated a by-ref body plus a "by-mut" clone plus a by-move body. The PR removes `by_mut_body`, renames the shared ref future to `CallRefFuture`, caps the coroutine kind so `Fn` and `FnMut` both use the by-ref body, and reserves the by-move body for `FnOnce`. It also fixes the confirmed bug that `Fn::call` on an async closure returned a body taking the receiver by move, and adjusts the `Fn`/`FnMut` shim ABI to take a pointer receiver while returning the `FnOnce`-flavored coroutine. Knowledge is assigned to `StateTransform` because the change concerns coroutine state-transform/by-move body generation and consumption. No compiler build or execution is claimed; conclusions come from the supplied diff and MIR test expectation changes.
analysis.originalLogic: Async closures had three trait-associated futures (`CallFuture`, `CallMutFuture`, `CallOnceFuture`) and mirrored that in body generation. `ByMoveBody` always produced a `by_move_body`; additionally, when the coroutine closure kind was `Fn`, it cloned the by-ref body into a `by_mut_body` whose `CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL` type was changed to a mutable-reference coroutine. `InstanceDef::ConstructCoroutineInClosureShim` and `InstanceDef::CoroutineKindShim` both carried a `target_kind`, and shim construction selected `FnMut` versus `FnOnce` flavors separately. Coroutine kind types were built with `Ty::from_closure_kind`, preserving all three closure kinds.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation keyed generated/selected coroutine bodies on all three closure kinds instead of only by-ref versus by-move. It constructed a redundant by-mut body as "actually just a copy of the by-ref body, but with a different self type", and the shim/body selection could consequently return a by-move body for the `Fn::call` path, taking the async-closure receiver by move. The fix caps `Fn`/`FnMut` to the same by-ref coroutine kind (`i16`) and uses the by-move body (`i32`) only for the `FnOnce` path. The `by_mut_body` is deleted rather than retained as a third body. Separately, the `Fn`/`FnMut` shim must still take its closure receiver by reference while returning the `FnOnce`-flavored coroutine, so the ABI is represented with `receiver_by_ref` and a `*mut Self` receiver.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust async closures / coroutine-closures and their `Fn`, `FnMut`, `FnOnce`, and unstable `AsyncFn*` MIR shims. Relevant inputs include captureless and capturing async closures invoked through `Fn::call`/`FnMut::call_mut`, through `AsyncFnOnce`, or through a generic `&impl Fn(i32) -> F`; the pass sees the coroutine body, its `by_move_body`, coroutine kind type, and the generated construct/kind shims. A two-program comparison should differ only in call path or closure kind (for example, a captureless async closure passed to `&impl Fn(i32) -> F` versus passed to `impl AsyncFnOnce(i32)`) so that by-ref versus by-move body selection is the only changed variable.
analysis.trigger: When building or selecting MIR bodies and ABI shims for an async closure whose closure kind is `Fn`/`FnMut` versus `FnOnce`, especially when `Fn::call`/`FnMut::call_mut` returns the `FnOnce`-flavored coroutine but must still borrow the closure receiver.
preconditions: The input is an async closure / coroutine-closure, not an ordinary coroutine or ordinary closure.
The coroutine has a by-move body generated by the by-move-body transform; only the by-ref and by-move bodies should be distinguished.
The `Fn`/`FnMut` shim path takes the closure receiver by reference but returns a coroutine whose kind is `FnOnce`.
The `receiver_by_ref` by-move/construct shim path expects no captures, asserted via `tupled_upvars_ty() == unit`.
pitfalls: Do not create or select a separate by-mut coroutine body: `Fn` and `FnMut` share the same by-ref body, and the old `by_mut_body` was literally a copy of the by-ref body with a different self type.
Do not populate the coroutine kind from `Ty::from_closure_kind` directly when constructing a coroutine from a coroutine-closure; cap `Fn` and `FnMut` together and keep only `FnOnce` distinct.
Do not use the by-move body for the `Fn::call` path; doing so takes the async-closure receiver by move and is the confirmed bug.
Deleting `by_mut_body` also requires removing its pass-manager recursion and its mirror/dump expectations; a retained old comment or test name does not by itself show the replacement is wrong.

Do not give the `Fn`/`FnMut` shim an exact by-value self signature: it only needs an ABI-compatible shim, using a mutable pointer to the closure receiver while returning the `FnOnce`-flavored coroutine.
The pointer-receiver construct shim is only valid without captures, so keep the unit-upvars assertion when `receiver_by_ref` is set.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the MIR-opt test `tests/mir-opt/async_closure_shims.rs` with `EMIT_MIR` for `coroutine_closure_by_move`, `coroutine_closure_by_ref`, and `coroutine_by_move`. The new by-ref test should show a pointer receiver, e.g. `_1: *mut {async closure...}`, and a coroutine construction using `move` for the argument. Add a generic `call_normal<F: Future<Output = ()>>(f: &impl Fn(i32) -> F)` path to exercise `Fn::call` on an async closure, alongside existing `call_mut` and `call_once` paths. Check that by-mut `EMIT_MIR` entries and `.coroutine_by_mut` files are gone. Update UI object-safety expectations (`tests/ui/async-await/async-fn/dyn-pos.rs`/`.stderr`): removing the `CallFuture` GAT should reduce duplicate `AsyncFn` object-safety errors, and `CallMutFuture` should become `CallRefFuture`. Also verify the by-move body is still emitted and used for the `FnOnce`/`AsyncFnOnce` path.
